tech.title: OpenAI Staffer Likely Captured Secrets on Hidden Bug, US Says
tech.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former engineer at OpenAI, has pleaded not guilty to an eavesdropping charge for bugging an office conference room, likely to intercept trade secrets. He has requested bail, but there are concerns that he may try to flee before trial given his relatively weak ties to the US and the considerable resources and connections he has to Saudi Arabia. The government has so far located hundreds of audio files on Alfozan's computer, many of which involve discussions of what may be trade secrets. He appears to have uploaded at least some of the recordings to Dropbox.

The mid-cycle refresh exists mainly because Tesla needs a new memory type it can actually buy. The cost of the AI4 chip is now twice as much due to memory and storage price hikes.

tech.title: The Incredible, Elegant DNA Repair System Makes Gene Editing Work

The mechanisms are essential to the evolutionary lineage of all known life. Scientists and doctors experimenting with gene editing use these natural self-editing and repair tools to insert, delete, or mutate genes to study and treat disease.

ai.title: Recursive Self-Editing: LLMs Program Their Own Weight Edits for Self-Improvement
ai.summary: Today's language models improve themselves through data, training recipes, or scaffolds. Whenever their weights change, gradient descent writes the update, not the model. SELFWRITE lets the model write its own weights. Each generation, the current model studies its own reasoning on fresh training problems, inspects its own weights and activations in a persistent Python session, and writes a program that constructs a low-rank weight edit for itself from white-box primitives. It can raise gate accuracy and accuracy on a held-out test split that the loop never sees without a single gradient step.

infosec.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
infosec.summary: binary-parser versions before 2.3.1 contain CVE-2026-134814, a code-injection flaw with CVSS scores of 9.2 and 8.1. An attacker who controls parser definitions can inject JavaScript through unvalidated string options, including length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, and namely() aliases. The code runs in the Node.js process when the parser compiles. Parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted definition is unaffected. Update to 2.3.1 or later.

infosec.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What's a Single Bit Between Friends?
infosec.summary: Clearing a single bit, the IMAGE_FILE_EXECUTABLE_IMAGE flag in a .NET assembly's PE header, makes NtCreateSection reject the file while the .NET Framework still loads it through a flat-image fallback that skips code integrity checks. Project Zero's James Forshaw used this to load untrusted code into hardened VirtualBox processes (CVE-2026-87268), bypass UMCI on Windows 11 S Mode through regasm.exe (CVE-2026-108398), and get TCB-level PPL code execution without admin rights by hijacking a COM object. Microsoft fixed the WLDP check in October, but the PPL bypass remains outside MSRC's servicing criteria, so defenders running WDAC should also enable the Dynamic Code Security option, which blocks the attack.

infosec.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
infosec.summary: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466 in clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E gateways. The flaw uses hard-coded credentials and weak certificate validation to gain unauthenticated root command execution. F6 observed two internet-facing devices compromised, then accessed two internal cluster nodes as attackers deployed Python scripts for SMB discovery, SQL Server and WinRM interaction, and GitLab credential searches. CISA added the 9.8-CVSS bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and set a Monday patch deadline for federal agencies.

infosec.title: Things LLMs Get Wrong About AWS IAM
infosec.summary: Writing AWS IAM permissions requires wading through a complex set of nuances. This post highlights three common anti-patterns that coding agents frequently trip over while writing policies. Agents often overuse Deny policies and permission boundaries, as well as unnecessarily include Allow statements for sts:GetCallerIdentity, which can never be denied.

infosec.title: Sandboxing AI Coding Agents: nono vs Docker Sandboxes vs Microsandbox vs OpenShell
infosec.summary: Kudelski Security tested nono, Docker Sandboxes, Microsandbox, and NVIDIA OpenShell for running AI coding agents safely. All four scored 4 to 4.5 out of 5. Docker Sandboxes and Microsandbox use microVMs, nono uses OS-level controls and starts fastest, and OpenShell supports several isolation backends. The review covers filesystem limits, network filtering, DNS rebinding, credential injection, resource controls, logging, and agent-specific profiles. Only nono and OpenShell scope credentials to both a domain and an endpoint. None can deny a file inside an allowed directory or customize allowed syscalls.

infosec.title: Supply Chain Compromise Backdoors Six WP Connect Plugins, Blocked by WordPress.org's Release Hold
infosec.summary: An attacker used WP Connect's own WordPress.org account to push backdoored releases of six plugins, including Air WP Sync and WP Sync for Notion, within about two hours. Each release added a fake "analytics and auto-update" module that checked in to tascredit-pay[.]com on every request with TLS verification turned off, ran whatever PHP the server sent back through eval(), and could also run shell commands, dump password hashes, and plant webshells. WordPress.org's new release cooling-off period under Protect The Shire stopped the updates before any site got them, and the developer says the account was compromised. However, admins should still check for the affected versions (CVE-2026-135202), remove them, and scan their sites for webshells and rogue WP-Cron hooks.

infosec.title: Introducing Mitigeddon: Real-world exploitation and prevalence data for impactful CVEs
infosec.summary: Mitigeddon, Datadog's new free site, shows how widespread each CVE is across real environments next to a timeline of its disclosure, public exploit release, and appearance in CISA or VulnCheck KEV. Datadog launched it with data showing that only 0.6 to 0.8% of CVEs are exploited in the wild, while the median time from disclosure to exploitation fell to 33 days in 2026 from 163 in 2024. The prevalence figures come from a sample of Datadog's own customer telemetry, so they lean toward cloud-native environments, but the site is still a useful way to filter out noise when prioritizing patches.

infosec.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted

At peak, it produced about 40 billion daily bid requests and over 4% of observed CTV traffic. Hidden modules spoofed legitimate apps, rendered invisible video ads, and enrolled devices in 11 residential proxy networks. Researchers linked parts of the operation to Chinese manufacturer TXCZ and to infrastructure disrupted during Google's XCPE takedown.

infosec.title: AI Agents Zip From Flaw Discovery to Root Access in 11 Minutes
infosec.summary: A China-linked actor used Cairn agents against East Asian universities for about 48 hours. The agents ran 148 actions against an exposed Redis server, tested over 30,000 SSH credential combinations against a GPU server, then found a path-traversal flaw in an open source medical imaging application. They wrote arbitrary files and ran a Python reverse shell as root within 11 minutes.

Oversized lettering extends across pizza boxes, menus, merchandise, and restaurant interiors, giving L'Artista an identity that feels closer to an independent hip-hop label than a conventional pizzeria.

design.title: Verve casts legacy software as the Stone Age in rebrand for AI startup Zero
design.summary: Amsterdam-based Verve has rebranded Helsinki AI startup Zero, positioning its software as an evolutionary leap that could make traditional customer relationship management platforms obsolete. The identity depicts legacy CRM systems as a prehistoric landscape of cracked earth and fossilized tools, contrasted with Zero's futuristic, alien-inspired technology and a character named Zorb. Designed as both a brand identity and an expandable campaign platform, the system combines unconventional creative concepts with AI-assisted production to support future marketing, events, and product communications.

design.title: Adobe's Democratization of Design Doesn't Have to Be the Death of Human Creativity
design.summary: Adobe MAX 2026 made clear that Adobe pitches its tools at everyone, from novices to industry veterans, deepening worries about AI slop and the value of craft.

marketing.title: Participation in Black Friday-Cyber Monday Shopping Expected to Hit 10-year High
marketing.summary: Deloitte reports that 87% of consumers plan to shop during BFCM this year, with average spending flat at $624. Gen Z leads with 94% planning to participate and $752 in expected spending, up 23% year over year. Social media and GenAI use are linked to higher spending, with shoppers using both expecting to spend 61% more than those using neither. Meanwhile, 72% are delaying some purchases in anticipation of better deals.

marketing.title: AI citations to social media & UGC grew 52% on Google's AI platforms, fell 44% on ChatGPT
marketing.summary: Citations to 18 UGC domains grew 52% across Google's AI platforms from January to August, but fell 44% on ChatGPT. YouTube led AI Overviews with 45% of tracked citations, while Reddit dominated ChatGPT at 52%. 17 of 18 sites gained citations on AI Overviews, while 12 lost citations on ChatGPT. TikTok saw the strongest growth across both. Despite low AI referral traffic of just 0.14%, UGC can shape brand visibility in AI answers. Citation patterns vary by category, making it important to identify which sources AI platforms reference most in your market.

marketing.title: How to make high-quality AI ads
marketing.summary: AI ads start with a product selling point and a customer pain point. Build a short story around one feature that solves a real problem, then test the hardest shot before generating the rest. AI reels often use a recognizable situation, an unusual opening frame, and a single product-focused payoff, usually within 15-30 seconds. Control the output by specifying shot sizes and color grading in consistent language. Generate short clips, make pacing and text adjustments in the edit, and change one prompt variable at a time.

marketing.title: The B2B demand gen checklist
marketing.summary: B2B companies can capture more existing buyer demand by improving how they handle high-intent leads. Route every demo and contact request to the right sales rep with instant booking or a response within 30 minutes. Track speed-to-lead as a KPI. Install ad pixels for retargeting and conversion tracking. Identify high-intent search and AI queries such as competitor comparisons and pricing. Target these through SEO, AEO, and paid search while organic rankings build.

marketing.title: SMB marketing report: paid social is up, SEO is down, and AI users are the majority
marketing.summary: Exclusive new data by LocaliQ looks at how small businesses are reevaluating their marketing investments amidst ongoing uncertainty. The results: 60% use AI for tasks like content creation; only 30% are investing in SEO; paid and organic social remain the main channels. See the data

marketing.title: Start Using AI in Communications Safely (Webinar)
marketing.summary: Get a practical intro to AI for communicators. Learn what it's good for, where it fails, and how to use it without sacrificing judgment. This free webinar will take place on November 26 at 9 AM PT.

marketing.title: Test Your Ecommerce Site for AI Access
marketing.summary: Ecommerce sites can test whether AI crawlers can access and read their content using 3 checks. A free tool from a former Google employee tests whether AI bots are blocked by robots.txt or server settings. Asking ChatGPT to find a sentence hidden in collapsible content can reveal whether it retrieves JavaScript-rendered text. Chrome Reading Mode offers another check by stripping away navigation and pop-ups to show whether key content such as product titles, descriptions, pricing, and reviews can be extracted cleanly.

marketing.title: New HubSpot data reveals how mentions and citations relate on the AI engine level
marketing.summary: Model releases now swing AI visibility the way algorithm updates once swung SEO. After an update to ChatGPT on August 6, cited URLs per prompt rose 51% and domain-specific searches rose 45x. Gemini's 3.7 Flash release cut citations per prompt 27% the same week it launched. Perplexity went the other way, doubling cited URLs per answer to about 18 while referral traffic fell 14%. Sources shifted too, with ChatGPT citing competitor sites more and forums and videos far less.

marketing.title: Can we design emotional loyalty?
marketing.summary: An emotional loyalty map treats loyalty as a series of moments, each with a specific emotion to design for. For every moment, from opening the app to a service failure, it compares what the member feels now with what they should feel and picks an action to close that gap. A new member opening the app may feel confused, so showing clear progress toward the next reward leaves them informed and motivated. After a service failure, the goal is reassurance, which comes from a fast fix and a reply that recognizes their membership.

marketing.summary: Dogfoodmaxxing means building content around how a company uses its own product.

marketing.title: Creativity Is Dying. And We're Replacing It With Creators

founders.title: How to Win Bots and Influence Purchases
founders.summary: Shoppers are starting to let AI agents pick products and software for them. a16z and The Prompting Company report over 11,000 controlled agent tests to see how they choose. Stores with better return terms won 86% of equal-price comparisons in those tests. Agents also finished guest checkout forms most of the time, while every checkout requiring a new account stopped early. Mandatory signups stopped those agents, so keep guest checkout open and make return terms easy to compare.

founders.title: Is SaaS Dead? The 8 Business Model Waves Behind the Debate
founders.summary: One way to compete with a leader is to pick a problem people already pay to solve and ride a new wave that the leader would lose money copying. This is called counter-positioning. This post looks at the eight waves of counter-positioning that have appeared since 1994. It covers how monetized open source helped Red Hat become the first open-source company to reach $1 billion in yearly revenue, how Amazon's hourly rentals cut into Sun Microsystems' server sales, and much more.

founders.title: Dogfoodmaxxing
founders.summary: The best content shows how companies use their products themselves. This is probably the most convincing way to market a product. Show people how a team can use a product for a real job, and customers will see what they could do with it as well. If your team can't use your own product, use it for a dream customer and send them the result.

founders.title: This is the most important AEO agent you need to be running right now
founders.summary: AI search engines already cite outside websites when answering buying questions, giving outreach teams specific pages to approach. A marketing agency linked an AI agent to a spreadsheet and team inbox to find cited pages and contact their editors. The agency reports sending 206 emails and landing 28 live mentions in its initial client test, while tracked AI citations also climbed. Start with a small batch of pages and review every draft before enabling autonomous sending, since a human should still handle any payment or commercial terms.

founders.title: Watching users is how you make products better
founders.summary: Few companies watch real people use their products anymore. Several people getting stuck in the same place marks a real problem, so repeat the sessions after a fix. Go where each person normally uses the product and let them use their own device. Give them a short script of basic tasks and ask them to think out loud while you say as little as possible.

crypto.title: CFTC staff say BTC and ETH can count toward derivatives firms' OpEx
crypto.summary: A staff advisory says swap execution facilities, clearing organizations, and designated contract markets may count BTC, ETH, and payment stablecoins, subject to a haircut, toward the requirement to hold a year of operating expenses. Crypto doesn't qualify as cash or very liquid securities, so it can't count toward the separate liquidity requirement, and the advisory isn't enforceable. The CFTC also published a final rule creating a reporting framework for certain event contracts, replacing no-action letters.

crypto.title: DOJ seeks $1.17 billion in USDC tied to Binance hack
crypto.summary: The DOJ filed a civil forfeiture complaint for about $1.17B in USDC across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains, attributing the theft on October 29 to North Korea's Lazarus Group/APT38, and separately asked a judge to keep the assets restrained since the November 12 order may lapse. Circle blocked the USDC but can't move the original tokens, so it agreed to issue equivalent new USDC to the US if forfeiture is granted. The DOJ says over $2.9B in crypto has been frozen, seized, or returned since the theft. Binance puts losses at about $6.34B, says it replenished them, and also won a $6.5B worldwide freezing order in Abu Dhabi.

crypto.title: Privy Adds Verifiable Enclave Attestations for Wallet Operations
crypto.summary: Privy added verifiable enclave attestations to its wallet infrastructure, giving developers cryptographic proof that sensitive wallet operations executed inside AWS Nitro enclaves. The feature shifts the security model from operator trust to cryptographic verification, letting any external party confirm that key operations ran in an isolated, hardened compute environment. This closes a gap common in MPC and embedded wallet providers, where users had to accept security claims without cryptographic evidence.

crypto.title: Visa Launches CLI Agent Wallet on Tempo and MPP
crypto.summary: Visa expanded its Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP) to agent wallets and task marketplaces, and launched Visa CLI, an experimental agent wallet for OUSD built on Tempo and the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), available to US users as a connector to major agent platforms. TAP lets users attach a Visa card to their agent wallet, register that agent in Visa's Agent Directory, and have the verified agent complete paid tasks spanning video creation, music, gaming, surveys, and market research, with earnings settled in OUSD. The expansion follows TAP's October 2025 debut and existing pilots with Cloudflare and Akamai for e-commerce authentication, plus a B2B pilot with Bill.com and Billtrust for agent-verified invoice payments. Visa is positioning its 5 billion existing payment credentials as the accountability layer for agent transactions and is soliciting integration partners among agent wallet builders, personal assistants, and marketplace operators.

crypto.summary: Agentic commerce is converging on the task, a verified unit of completed work. This article outlines three layers: single agent with skills and MCP, pay-per-call, and task markets for complex work needing judgement and verification. Coinbase is building open standards on its own rails while Stripe is closed and extends its existing business, with Tempo as the settlement layer that could weaken harness lock-in. Daydreams' TaskMarket on Base and Tempo (ERC-8195) has 16,500 registered agents, 1,843 tasks, and about $3,756 paid out, and Visa's new CLI wallet integrates it.

crypto.title: What's a Block, and How Big Can It Get?
crypto.summary: Under Glamsterdam's 60M gas limit, skipped EIP-7702 authorizations, not calldata, represent the worst-case block-size attack vector, packing 17.0 bytes per 1k gas and producing 1.81 MiB EL blocks, about 2x what calldata can achieve. This creates a structural conflict with FOCIL (EIP-7805): a transaction satisfying gas constraints may breach the 8 MiB EL byte cap when appended, leaving builders unable to honor attesters' inclusion expectations despite valid gas usage. The proposed re-encoding patch fails in four edge cases, so the author argues for pricing every payload byte in gas via EIP-8131 and EIP-8279 plus deposit-request metering, with a capped gas limit (256M without those EIPs, 500M with them). This bounds worst-case envelope size and gives the CL a deterministic maximum: max_envelope_size = C + ceil(1.25 x gas_limit / 64).

crypto.title: How Can Crypto Neobanks Win?
crypto.summary: Weekly crypto card spend exceeds $300M, up almost 200% year over year, but the top 5 of the 20 largest programs hold 86% of the last 30 days' spend, with RedotPay alone over 46%. Users spend only $0.65 to $0.75 per $1 topped up, treating apps as savings, and EtherFi and KAST offer 7 to 9% APY on stablecoin deposits. After cashback, most programs earn under 1% of spend while paying 2 to 3%, and card infrastructure from providers like Rain is commoditized. Differentiation will come from local rails, multi-currency settlement, and owning the yield source, with EtherFi's Aave V4 loans over $47M and Phantom earning over $20M in perps builder fees.

crypto.title: XMR1 Collapses 99% After Deployer Key Stolen in Web Host Breach
crypto.summary: XMR1, Wagyu's wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid, fell from about $500 to $1 in 30 minutes after an attacker extracted 5.2 million tokens from the deployer wallet and sold 364,000 of them to 388 buyers for $13.5 million, converting the proceeds to about 7,350 ETH. Wagyu founder PerpetualCow attributed the breach to Icelandic host 1984.hosting, claiming the deployer private key persisted on a deleted server whose logs the host retained, with 1984 confirming a broad cyberattack on its infrastructure without naming Wagyu or disclosing whether customer data was taken. The attacker seeded the exploit wallet via Tornado Cash minutes before the drain, and the same deployer account still controls ZEC1, a wrapped Zcash token carrying identical centralization risk. PerpetualCow pledged direct refunds to affected holders with no relaunch timeline given. The incident is Wagyu's second reported breach in two months and follows the service's appearance in ZachXBT's tracing of a $106 million theft routed through the platform.

crypto.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post $1.79B Weekly Outflow, Third-Largest on Record
crypto.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $1.79B in net outflows last week, the third-largest weekly total since the product category launched in January 2024, extending a four-week redemption streak to $4.34B.

crypto.title: Lessons learned from 15 years in crypto
crypto.summary: Focus on reality over the perception game, since many once-legit founders and VCs have come and gone, and take the other side when the timeline is shilling a narrative.

it.title: Europe Pushes for Cloud Sovereignty Amid US Dominance
it.summary: European governments and regulated industries are increasingly incorporating digital sovereignty requirements into cloud procurement contracts to reduce dependence on US technology providers. Although high-profile contracts have been awarded to European and hybrid providers, overall migration remains slow due to strong incumbent lock-in and high migration friction.

it.title: Jensen Huang returns as CEO of Nvidia
it.summary: Nvidia's board has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his resignation following consultations with senior US government officials. The board determined that his reinstatement does not pose a national security risk. Huang's return reduces immediate leadership uncertainty at a critical point in the global AI infrastructure buildout.

it.title: CrowdStrike to purchase Zscaler for $43.9 billion
it.summary: CrowdStrike has announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, bringing endpoint protection, zero-trust networking, cloud security, and threat intelligence under one platform. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue leading the business and join CrowdStrike's board. The deal represents a major step toward security platform consolidation and could reshape enterprise security purchasing decisions.

it.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
it.summary: Microsoft's final incident report reveals how a Windows defect went undetected for months before overwhelming Microsoft 365 gateway servers. At its peak, more than 80% of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. Microsoft identified gaps in load testing, failover procedures, and infrastructure capacity, and plans to improve service isolation and recovery mechanisms.

it.title: AI is changing the build-versus-buy equation. Are CIOs ready?
it.summary: AI-powered development tools and vibe coding reduce software creation costs but do not eliminate ongoing security, maintenance, and integration expenses. CIOs should selectively reconsider building specialized, non-critical SaaS applications rather than replacing core enterprise platforms, especially as AI tools can introduce security risks without necessarily improving development productivity.

it.title: Should Apple really move fast and break things?
it.summary: As Apple faces pressure to accelerate its AI development, its deliberate engineering culture could be a competitive advantage. Introducing unreliable AI capabilities at the operating system level carries greater consequences than standalone chatbot errors, making reliability, privacy, and customer trust particularly important.

it.title: How AI impacted the release of Postgres 19
it.summary: AI-assisted testing uncovered numerous defects during PostgreSQL 19 development, contributing to its delayed release. The experience highlights an emerging engineering challenge: while AI accelerates development and bug discovery, human validation, architectural decisions, and quality assurance remain critical bottlenecks.

it.title: 📊 How many dashboards is too many?
it.summary: Every new monitoring tool, service, or "quick integration" adds another dashboard to the pile—and before you know it, you're spending more time switching between tools than actually building. With Microsoft Azure , your entire stack lives in one workspace: infrastructure, data, AI, and more. See how Azure brings it all together →

it.title: AWS Systems Manager Automation now automates operational tasks in Azure and Google Cloud
it.summary: AWS has expanded Systems Manager Automation to support multicloud environments. IT teams can centrally automate configuration remediation, resource cleanup, agent deployment, and infrastructure changes without maintaining separate automation workflows across cloud providers.

it.title: CloudWatch Omni
it.summary: Amazon has launched CloudWatch Omni, an AI-powered observability solution built on open standards and delivered outside the AWS Console. The platform unifies the monitoring and evaluation of AI agents, applications, and infrastructure across multi-account environments. Designed for development workflows, it integrates directly into IDEs and provides features like auto-discovered topology, natural-language querying, and continuous trace evaluations.

it.title: Workday Completes Acquisition of C1.ai
it.summary: Workday has completed its acquisition of C1.ai, formerly ConductorOne, expanding into identity governance. Combining employee lifecycle data with access management capabilities will help organizations automate provisioning, permission management, and security enforcement for employees and AI agents.

it.title: Tokenless AI: Slackbot Powered by Claude
it.summary: Slack has introduced Slackbot powered by Claude, offering flat-rate pricing per person on Enterprise+ plans to eliminate per-token usage costs for everyday AI tasks. The company argues that tokenless pricing helps organizations avoid unpredictable AI bills and lets employees use AI freely without rationing adoption. Early users report significant reductions in overage charges and improved workflow efficiency by routing routine queries through Slackbot.

it.title: How Security Vendors Are Tackling Access-Control Challenges for AI Agents
it.summary: Security vendors are introducing a range of access-control, monitoring, and testing tools to address the unique challenges posed by autonomous enterprise AI agents. Companies such as CrowdStrike, Okta, and Cisco are deploying new capabilities to prevent agents from executing unauthorized actions or falling victim to confused-deputy scenarios. At the same time, industry groups like the Blueprint Alliance are attempting to coordinate standards across vendors for securing agent identities and tasks.

it.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
it.summary: Amazon is acquiring Decart's AI optimization technology and engineering talent to improve hardware utilization across Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and AWS Trainium chips, targeting faster inference, higher throughput, and lower AI computing costs.

it.title: New Outlook's attachment issues sent users into the arms of its predecessor
it.summary: Microsoft recommends switching to classic Outlook or its web client after a software update broke attachment handling.

it.title: AWS CodeDeploy now supports suspending Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling processes
it.summary: AWS introduces controls to temporarily suspend Auto Scaling activities during application deployments, preventing instances from being replaced mid-update.
